artifacts.summary: Confirms lake-build-guard.sh's finalize_record() is unreached on a killed/cancelled holder path (no trap), while decide_sharing() and flock's own release-on-exit semantics already correctly prevent an in_flight/dead-holder record from being shared or blocking a waiter. Recommends a trap-based terminal 'aborted' state (idempotency-guarded), documents the SIGKILL and bash deferred-trap-execution limits affecting both the fix and its test, and lays out the absorbed result-subcommand/--expect-pid/--expect-scope/STATUS-line design that depends on the new terminal state.

memory_candidates.content: bash defers execution of an EXIT/INT/TERM trap until the current foreground command returns. A script that runs a wrapped command in the foreground (e.g. lake-build-guard.sh's run_lake_foreground()) will not have its trap fire promptly if only the top-level script PID is signalled while the wrapped child keeps running -- the signal must reach the whole process group/cgroup (as Ctrl-C or a systemd scope kill naturally does) for the child to die first and the trap to then run. Relevant to any trap-based cleanup/finalization design and to writing a test that kills a holder process mid-work.

flock(2) advisory locks are released when the last file descriptor referencing the open file description closes, across all processes, including on SIGKILL of the holding process -- no explicit unlock or PID bookkeeping is needed for a waiter to unblock after a holder dies. This means a waiter blocked on `flock -w` never needs a separate holder-liveness check to avoid hanging; only a DIRECT reader of an on-disk state record (bypassing the lock) needs a terminal-state guarantee.
